name: Hugging Face
license: Proprietary service; the `huggingface_hub` client and `hf` CLI, and the Transformers library, are Apache 2.0
summary: The main public host for open model weights, datasets and demo apps, stored as Git repositories on a chunk-deduplicating storage layer, with a pay-as-you-go router that sends API calls to partner inference providers.
intro: Every model, dataset and Space on the Hub is a Git repository, with commit history, branches, diffs and pull requests. Large binaries such as Safetensors weights or Parquet files don’t live in Git itself: Git keeps a small pointer file and the bytes sit in remote storage on Amazon S3. That storage layer is now Xet, from the Seattle startup Hugging Face bought in August 2024. Git LFS, which the Hub used before, stores whole files, so adding one row to a 10 GB Parquet file meant uploading 10 GB again; Xet splits files into chunks and uploads only the chunks that changed. Xet has been the default for new accounts since 23 May 2025. The `huggingface_hub` Python library and its `hf` CLI download into a local cache that Transformers and other libraries share, and `--revision` pins a download to a commit, branch or tag.

Model repositories carry a model card, a README with metadata such as tasks, languages and evaluation results. Spaces host demo apps built with Gradio, static HTML or Docker, on free CPU Basic hardware (2 vCPU, 16 GB) or on GPUs billed by the hour, from $0.40 for an Nvidia T4. Inference Providers puts one OpenAI-compatible endpoint, `https://router.huggingface.co/v1`, in front of partners such as Cerebras, Groq, Together and Replicate. A suffix on the model id picks the route: `:fastest` (the default, highest tokens per second), `:cheapest` (lowest price per output token), `:preferred` (your own order) or a provider name such as `:groq`. Hugging Face says it adds no markup to provider rates; a PRO account ($9 a month) includes $2 of inference credits a month.

On 3 September 2026 Nvidia announced an agreement to buy Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, expected to close in the first half of 2027 subject to regulatory approval. Nvidia counted more than 18 million users sharing over 3 million models, 500,000 datasets and 1 million apps, and said the Hub would stay open to every model maker, cloud and accelerator, with no requirement to use Nvidia hardware.
strengths: Git semantics for model weights and datasets: history, branches, diffs and pull requests, and any download can be pinned to an exact revision
Chunk-level deduplication with Xet, so an updated checkpoint or an appended dataset uploads only the changed bytes instead of whole files
Free public hosting and 100 GB of free private storage; paid plans add private storage at $18 per TB-month, with egress and CDN included at no extra cost
One Hugging Face token reaches many inference providers through an OpenAI-compatible router, with no markup on provider rates
limits: Free public storage is best effort beyond “the first few gigabytes”: Hugging Face asks that large uploads be useful to the community and sends heavy users to PRO, Team or Enterprise plans
The Git structure still shows: Hugging Face recommends fewer than 100,000 files per repository, 10,000 entries per folder and 200 GB per file
Inference Providers only serves models that a partner chooses to host, and it is pay-as-you-go beyond the monthly credits in paid plans
Ownership is changing: Nvidia’s purchase, announced in September 2026, is due to close in the first half of 2027

snippet.title: Download weights with the hf CLI, then call a model through Inference Providers
source: pip install -U huggingface_hub        # the hf CLI, plus hf_xet for Xet storage
hf auth login                         # paste a token from hf.co/settings/tokens
hf download gpt2 config.json          # one file into ~/.cache/huggingface/hub
# OpenAI-compatible router; the suffix picks the provider policy

story: Clément Delangue, Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf founded Hugging Face in New York in 2016, named after the hugging face emoji, to build a chatbot app for teenagers. TechCrunch’s 2017 review described a digital friend you texted for fun, not an assistant. The company later open-sourced the model behind the chatbot and turned to tools for machine learning.

Its Transformers library, described in a 2019 paper, put many pretrained Transformer architectures behind one API, backed by “a curated collection of pretrained models made by and available for the community.” In 2020 Hugging Face built the first version of the Hub on Git and Git LFS because LFS was well known and a reasonable way to start. By 2024 it held 12 PB in LFS across 280 million files and served 6 PB a day, and LFS was never meant for files that large, so in August 2024 Hugging Face bought XetHub, whose founders had built Apple’s internal ML infrastructure, to replace it.

The Hub grew from model hosting into datasets, Spaces for demo apps, GPU jobs, storage buckets and a router to partner inference providers. On 3 September 2026 Nvidia agreed to buy the company for $12.93 billion, saying Hugging Face would keep its brand and stay open to every model, cloud and accelerator.

choices.choice: Git repositories for models and datasets
choices.why: Versioning, history and pull requests came with Git, and Git LFS was well known enough to bootstrap the Hub in 2020.

choices.choice: Replace Git LFS with Xet’s chunked storage
choices.why: AI files are very large and change a little at a time: with LFS, adding one row to a 10 GB Parquet file meant uploading 10 GB again, while chunk deduplication sends only the new chunks.

choices.choice: Free public storage, paid private storage
choices.why: Hugging Face wants to give the community generous free space for public work and charges for private repositories above a free tier.
Instead of one provider’s catalog, one token and one OpenAI-compatible API reach many providers, with no markup on their rates.

timeline.text: Founded in New York to build a chatbot app
First version of the Hub, built on Git and Git LFS
Buys XetHub to replace Git LFS (August)
Xet becomes the default storage for new users and organizations (23 May)
Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face for $12.93 billion (3 September)
